clue.text: Top churchman, perhaps local one?

parts.note: a cardinal is a senior prince of the Roman Catholic Church
a local anaesthetic is something that numbs, read playfully as a numb-er

explanation.surface: A question whether a senior cleric might also serve as the neighbourhood priest.
explanation.walkthrough: NUMBER is read as 'numb-er', a thing that numbs, as a local anaesthetic does; the '?' flags that pun and the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure 'one' is an example of a counting figure such as one, two, three, as opposed to first, second.

clue.text: Small part from old English computer turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning the pieces upwards means writing them bottom to top

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: A minor role turns out to have come from an antique English computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief appearance by a well-known actor in a film or play is a minor role of this kind.

clue.text: Equal ops watchdog controlled by right-wing scoundrel? Come again?

indicators.note: the watchdog is held in the grip of the other pieces, so they surround it

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a cur is a contemptible man, a rotter
the EOC was Britain's Equal Opportunities Commission

explanation.surface: A rights watchdog falls under the control of a right-wing rogue, prompting a startled 'Come again?'
explanation.walkthrough: The EOC was the UK body that policed equal opportunities. 'Come again?' looks like a request to repeat something; here it is the plain verb, to happen once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To happen a second time is a direct synonym for recur after an earlier occurrence.

clue.text: She's in my view, you 'ear, increasingly frigid

indicators.note: a dropped-aitch 'you hear' says the phrase is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: saying she is in sight gives 'I see her', with the h dropped as 'I see 'er'

explanation.surface: A Cockney speaker remarks that a woman in sight is growing ever colder.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H in 'you 'ear' hints that 'her' should also lose its H, so 'I see 'er' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Colder still, more like frozen water: the comparative of a word meaning chilly or frosty.

clue.text: Put into practice, program gave inaccurate data

parts.note: an app is a software program
to give false information is to have lied

explanation.surface: Software deployed in practice turns out to have produced faulty figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Theory that has been used in real work is described as having been implemented or employed.

clue.text: 'Remembrance of Things Past' again lost in translation

indicators.note: translating rewrites words in a new form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Proust's novel title, as rendered in English, loses something once more in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remembrance of Things Past' is the old English title of Proust's novel, but here it is simply read as a description of a feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A wistful longing for the past is exactly a recollecting of things gone by.

clue.text: Payment one's picked up, being top in Tour de France

definitions.text: being top in Tour de France

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the pieces means reading them from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge paid, as for a road or bridge
'one's' expands to 'I am' when the speaker is the one

explanation.surface: A cyclist's payment is collected on becoming leader in the Tour de France.
explanation.walkthrough: The race leader wears the maillot jaune, the yellow jersey; 'top' is a garment, not first place.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is the French word for a cycling jersey, the garment worn on the upper body in the Tour.

clue.text: River crustacean the French find loathsome

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a crab is a shelled sea creature
le is the French masculine for 'the'

explanation.surface: The French find a river crab revolting to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detestable or appalling in quality is described by this strong word of disgust.

clue.text: One encountering measure of resistance rejected expression of false modesty initially?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the unit is written backwards

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone meeting resistance spurns a modest-sounding remark from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' is part of the definition: the answer is a set of initials, standing for 'in my humble opinion'.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet shorthand for 'in my humble opinion', often a show of humility before a firm view.

clue.text: Independent politician behind fourth estate terminally unfeeling

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
ass is slang for the backside
IV is the Roman numeral for four

indicators.note: terminally means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: An independent MP lags behind a press that is ultimately heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fourth estate' reads as the press, but it splits: 'fourth' gives IV, and 'estate terminally' gives its last letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing no emotion or reaction, impassive describes someone who seems not to feel.

clue.text: Musical performance using key instrument

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance
playing in the key of A, so 'in A'

explanation.surface: A concert performed using one key instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hexagonal bellows-driven squeezebox is a musical instrument of the accordion family.

clue.text: In grip of regressive Uzbek ruler, keep low profile

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left
the letters are held within the grip of the two words

explanation.surface: Under a backward-looking Central Asian strongman, it pays to stay out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait unseen or stay quietly in the background is to avoid attention.

clue.text: Put in military unit to capture western-inclined African state, held using arms

indicators.note: capturing means holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a journalist embedded is placed with a military unit

indicators.note: in an across entry, leaning west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: CAR is the Central African Republic

explanation.surface: A reporter placed with troops seizes a pro-Western African country, holding it by force of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using arms' suggests weapons, but here it means the limbs, as in a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug someone is to hold them closely in one's arms.

clue.text: Pass degree at university

parts.note: a measure is an amount or degree, as in 'a measure of success'
being up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: Someone passing their degree at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' suggests a qualification; here it is an extent. 'Up' for being at university is a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet the required standard is to pass, as one passes an inspection.

clue.text: Titled officer, one in papers

parts.note: Capt is the abbreviation for captain

indicators.note: the number word sits inside the documents, between their letters

parts.note: ID is identity papers
the number word taken as it is

explanation.surface: An officer with a title, one featured in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titled' suggests a noble officer, but it means given a heading or label.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture given a title or explanatory line underneath has been labelled in this way.

clue.text: Novel millionaire happy about bank being revived

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the bank

parts.note: gay in its old sense means merry or happy
TSB, the Trustee Savings Bank, was brought back as a separate high-street brand

explanation.surface: A fictional millionaire is cheerful about his bank's revival.
explanation.walkthrough: TSB is a British high-street bank whose brand was revived around the time of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Gatsby is the rich title character of F. Scott Fitzgerald's novel 'The Great Gatsby'.

clue.text: Artificially inflate male animal's offspring

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a pup is the young of a dog or seal

explanation.surface: Someone exaggerates the worth of a ram's lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp a price is to push it up by artificial means, and to raise output or prices rapidly.

clue.text: Cooking expert? One that can make anything better

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: the thing that cures all

parts.note: a pan is the vessel used in cooking
an ace is an expert
a is one

explanation.surface: A query about a master chef, someone whose cooking improves everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking expert?' looks like a definition but is two pieces: PAN, the cooking pot, and ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cure-all or universal remedy is thought to fix every problem or illness.

clue.text: Faker showed sign of injury, walked unsteadily

parts.note: a sham is a fraud or pretender
a wound that bled shows injury

explanation.surface: A fraud faking a wound limped about.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuffle along awkwardly or clumsily is to move with an unsteady gait.

clue.text: Coordinated action from majority of church body and two-thirds of ordained members

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its last two letters dropped

parts.note: a synod is a church council

indicators.note: four of the six letters are kept, the first two dropped

parts.note: the clergy are the ordained ministers of a church

explanation.surface: A church council and most of its priests pull together in joint effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Combined effort producing more than the parts alone is cooperative interaction between agents.

clue.text: Dish from India flying in by air

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed about in the air and landing reordered

explanation.surface: An Indian meal arrives by air freight.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced rice dish layered with meat or vegetables, from the Indian subcontinent.

clue.text: One in five gets just over halfway through malaria treatment

indicators.note: stopping a little past the middle keeps four of the seven letters

parts.note: quinine is the classic drug for malaria

explanation.surface: A patient gets a little more than half their malaria course.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintuplet, one of five babies born at a single birth, is shortened this way.

clue.text: Not a calculating type, earn minute rent

indicators.note: rent as a past participle means torn apart, so the letters are pulled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone bad with money earns a tiny rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like a noun for payment; here it means ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without basic arithmetic skill cannot work out sums, the counterpart of illiterate.

clue.text: Jock, son of a prostitute

definitions.note: a noun: a muscular, sporty man of brash masculinity

parts.note: Mac in Scottish surnames means 'son of'
ho is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a Scotsman, calling him the son of a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jock' suggests a Scot, which fits MAC, but it is the definition: an athletic tough guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering, sporty man, typically one flaunting strength and toughness, is a he-man type.

clue.text: A Lloyd Webber's former partner's second

definitions.meaning: lyricist Tim Rice, written as initial and surname like 'A Lloyd Webber'

explanation.surface: A note on how long Andrew Lloyd Webber's old collaborator took.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Lloyd Webber wrote musicals with lyricist Tim Rice; given as initial plus surname, 'T Rice' runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant, as in 'back in a jiffy', is a very brief moment of time.

clue.text: Odd to be so focused on Brussels?

parts.note: EC is the European Commission, based in Brussels
-centric means centred on, as in Eurocentric

explanation.surface: A jibe that being fixated on Brussels and the EU is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional or peculiar in behaviour, off centre from the norm.

clue.text: Drought-hit region's first to get external help

indicators.note: the help goes outside, wrapping round the single letter

parts.note: aid is help

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A region suffering drought is the first to receive foreign aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Land without rain is parched and dry, so a place suffering water shortage is described so.

clue.text: Lifting phone and climbing higher to improve reception on social network?

definitions.text: climbing higher to improve reception on social network

parts.note: raising something moves it upwards
a mobile is a cell phone

explanation.surface: Someone holds a phone aloft and climbs higher to get a better signal on a social site.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays both ways: climbing for a better phone signal, and rising in the social ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone rising in social and economic status is said to be climbing the social ladder.
